reduction.quote:
A positive integer that never increases and starts above $1$ can never reach $1$; hence
$P > 1$ after any number of moves.
reduction.witness: COUNTEREXAMPLE: the sequence of positive integers $P_0=2$, $P_1=1$ is non-increasing and starts above $1$, yet reaches $1$. Thus monotonicity alone does not prove that the board product remains greater than $1$.
reduction.load_bearing: This is the written justification that at least one entry greater than $1$ survives. Without it, the argument establishes finite termination and at most one surviving nonunit, but not exactly one.

upper_bound.quote:
By part (a), every play ends in the position $(1, 1, \dots, 1, M)$ (up to the order of the
places).
upper_bound.witness: The missing statement is that every legal play, in all cases, terminates with a unique entry $M>1$ rather than with all entries equal to $1$. This passage merely invokes part (a), whose only proof of survival uses the false monotonicity claim; therefore the terminal decoding is proved only under an unproved assumption.
upper_bound.load_bearing: Identifying $G_p$ with $v_p(M)$, and hence proving that the final value is choice-independent, requires the existence of that unique terminal nonunit.

parsed.notes: Mapping: reduction = finite termination with one nonunit; lower_bound = prime-valuation gcd invariance; upper_bound = decoding that invariant at the unique-nonunit terminal board.
